The exchange

The PTC Youth Exchange is an international artistic and educational programme bringing together advanced young musicians and vocalists from Germany, Austria and Finland for an intensive exploration of Present-Time Composition (PTC). Over ten days of collective learning, artistic experimentation and shared living, participants will explore new possibilities for improvisation and composition.

The central aim of the exchange is to enrich participants’ existing musical abilities by introducing them to PTC. Through practical exercises and ensemble work, participants will develop greater awareness of their creative impulses, deepen their listening skills and discover new ways of making musical decisions together in the present moment.

Alongside musical improvisation, the exchange will incorporate movement practices inspired by PTC_Dance, extending the exploration of creative impulses and collective interaction beyond sound. Participants will be invited to engage with both music and movement, investigating how physical awareness, embodied expression and non-verbal communication can enrich their artistic practice.

Beyond individual artistic development, the project emphasises collective experience. Participants from different musical, cultural and educational backgrounds will work, learn and live together, creating opportunities for intercultural exchange and lasting connections.

What is PTC?

Programme and methodology

The exchange will take place from 18 to 28 February 2027, with 18 February designated as the arrival day and 28 February as the departure day.

The work will move between individual exploration, partner and small-group exercises, ensemble improvisation and movement practices. By approaching improvisation through both sound and physical movement, participants will have opportunities to develop a deeper understanding of their creative processes and discover connections between musical and bodily expression.

The methodology emphasises learning through direct experience. Rather than focusing on theoretical instruction alone, participants will develop their understanding through practical experimentation, attentive listening, physical awareness, immediate feedback and collective reflection.

Participants

The exchange is intended for advanced musicians and vocalists between the ages of 18 and 30 who reside in Germany, Austria or Finland.

Participants should have a strong musical background and an interest in exploring improvisation, collective composition and new approaches to artistic creativity.

The programme incorporates both PTC_Music and PTC_Dance. Participants should therefore be open to actively engaging in movement-based practices alongside musical activities. Previous dance training or experience is not required. Previous experience with PTC is not required.

Participants do not need to hold citizenship of an EU member state. Eligibility is based on residence in one of the three participating countries.

Living and learning together

A central element of the PTC Youth Exchange is the experience of building a temporary community. Throughout the programme, participants will live and work together at The Other Music Academy (OMA) in Weimar, Germany.

The OMA building will serve as both the artistic workspace and the shared living environment. Participants will sleep on-site, prepare meals together and take collective responsibility for everyday activities such as cooking, cleaning and maintaining the shared spaces. This communal approach is an integral part of the exchange.

The experience of living together creates opportunities for informal exchange, personal connections and shared learning beyond the scheduled working sessions. It also reflects important aspects of PTC itself: attentive listening, cooperation, individual responsibility and awareness of one’s role within a collective.

Erasmus+ and non-formal learning

The project takes place within the framework of Erasmus+ Youth Exchanges, which support non-formal learning, intercultural dialogue and the active participation of young people. In addition to artistic development, the exchange provides opportunities to experience cooperation, shared responsibility and collective decision-making in an international environment.

The communal living structure further supports these values by involving participants in decisions and responsibilities concerning everyday life together. In this way, the exchange connects artistic practice with broader experiences of participation, cooperation and intercultural understanding.

Costs and participation fee

Travel, accommodation and subsistence costs are covered by the host organisation, The Other Music Academy e.V. (OMA), within the framework of the Erasmus+ programme.

A participation fee of €100 per participant is required. All other programme-related costs are covered.

We believe that financial circumstances should not prevent anyone from taking part. If the participation fee presents a financial difficulty, participants are encouraged to contact us so that we can find a suitable solution together.

Apply

Participants are selected through an open call. Applications can be submitted via the online form from 1 to 15 December 2026, and selected participants will be notified in the first week of January 2027.

We warmly welcome applications from people of all genders, ethnicities, nationalities, migration backgrounds, religions and beliefs, sexual orientations, abilities, and social and economic backgrounds. Diverse perspectives and experiences are at the heart of collective creation, and we are committed to making the exchange a respectful and inclusive space for everyone.

If you have any questions about the application or need support with access, please get in touch. We are happy to help.
